title: Finite lifting tests recognize the natural Cartesian marking
statement: Use marked simplicial sets and the finite maps (i), (ii), (iii) and $A^\flat\to A$ of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], and arbitrary-base cartesian fibrations and natural markings of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]. Let $S$ be any small simplicial set. Let $J_S$ consist of every map of types (i), (ii), (iii) equipped with every simplicial map from its codomain to $S$, and of $A_s^\flat\to A_s$ for each vertex $s\in S_0$, where both base maps are constant at $s$. For a small marked map $p:(X,M)\to S^\sharp$, the following conditions are equivalent: (a) every commutative square with left side in $J_S$ and right side $p$ admits a marked diagonal over $S$; (b) $X\to S$ is a cartesian fibration and $M$ is exactly its set of cartesian edges. No quasicategory hypothesis on $S$ or $X$ and no relative model structure is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7, proof of (1), printed pp.158-159: finite detector and recognition of j_X; Proposition 3.1.1.6 and Remark 3.1.1.10 for the horn argument. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result.

proof.text: Assume (a). For each inner-horn generator of type (i), choose the displayed map of its codomain to S; a lift is exactly an inner-horn filler for p, so p is an inner fibration. For an edge alpha:s→p(y) of S, use a type-(ii) generator with n=1 and the codomain map alpha, sending its final vertex to y. Because S^sharp marks every edge, the resulting diagonal is a marked edge e':y'→y over alpha. This is the prescribed-target lifting condition. For n≥2, the same type-(ii) generators say that every marked edge of X satisfies the final-horn cartesian criterion. Thus p is a cartesian fibration in the arbitrary-base sense of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], and every marked edge is p-cartesian.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7, proof of (1), printed p.158: 'Arguing as in the proof of Proposition 3.1.1.6 ... j_X is an inner fibration, every marked edge is j_X-Cartesian, ... there exists a marked edge lifting'; Proposition 3.1.1.6, proof, first paragraph.

proof.text: Fiber identification. Fix a vertex $s\in S_0$, let $X_s=X\times_S\{s\}$ be the degreewise fiber and $M_s=M\cap(X_s)_1$, which contains the degenerate edges. (1) Assume (a). A commutative square from a map $K\to L$ of $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{fin}}$ (types (i), (ii), (iii) and $A^\flat\to A$) to $(X_s,M_s)\to(\Delta^0)^\sharp$ is the same as a square from the member of $J_S$ with base map $L\to S$ constant at $s$ to $p$, because $p$ maps the top arrow into $X_s$ exactly when the bottom arrow is constant at $s$; a marked diagonal over $S$ of the latter lands in $X_s$ and is a diagonal of the former. So $(X_s,M_s)\to(\Delta^0)^\sharp$ has the right lifting property against $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and [lem-coef-finite-marked-fibrancy-criterion] shows that $X_s$ is a quasicategory and $M_s$ is exactly its set of equivalences. (2) Assume only that $p$ is a cartesian fibration, with $N$ its set of cartesian edges. The pullback clause of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus] for $a:\Delta^0\to S$ at $s$ says that $X_s\to\Delta^0$ is a cartesian fibration whose cartesian edges are exactly $N_s=N\cap(X_s)_1$. The first clause of the same node, for the base $\Delta^0$, gives $(X_s,N_s)\to(\Delta^0)^\sharp$ the right lifting property against every marked-anodyne map. The point characterization in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] then says that $(X_s,N_s)=C^\natural$ for a quasicategory $C$, necessarily $C=X_s$; thus $N_s$ is exactly the set of equivalences of $X_s$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7, proof of (1), printed p.159: 'Since e0 and e are both j_X-Cartesian, the map f0 is an equivalence in T(X)_s' and the extension property for A^flat_s -> A_s; Proposition 3.1.1.6, proof (the largest Kan complex in X_{p(x)}); the details the source omits are written here.

proof.text: Assume (a); we show that every cartesian edge is marked. Step 1 makes $p$ a cartesian fibration with $M\subseteq N$. Fix $e\in N$, $e:y_0\to y$ over $\alpha:s\to t$. Step 1 gives $e'\in M$, $e':y_1\to y$ over $\alpha$. Since $e'$ is cartesian, the final-horn criterion for $n=2$ (horn with $d_0=e'$, $d_1=e$, base $s_0(\alpha)$) gives a $2$-simplex $\sigma$ of $X$ with $d_0\sigma=e'$, $d_1\sigma=e$ and $p(\sigma)=s_0(\alpha)$. Its edge $u=d_2\sigma:y_0\to y_1$ lies over $d_2s_0(\alpha)=s_0(s)$, hence in $X_s$. By [lem-coef-marked-triangle-cancellation] the identity map $(\Delta^2,\{\text{degenerate},[0,2],[1,2]\})\to(\Delta^2)^\sharp$ is marked anodyne (its class $W$ is generated by the same four families as in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]). The square given by $\sigma$ into $(X,N)$ and $p(\sigma)$ into $S^\sharp$ therefore has a marked diagonal by the first clause of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]; the diagonal is $\sigma$ itself, so $u\in N$. Hence $u\in N_s$, which by Step 2(2) is the set of equivalences of $X_s$, which by Step 2(1) is $M_s$. So $u\in M$. Now $\sigma$ has $d_2\sigma=u$ and $d_0\sigma=e'$ in $M$, so it defines a square from the type-(iii) map, with base map $p(\sigma)$, to $p$; the lift marks $d_1\sigma=e$. Thus $N\subseteq M$, and with Step 1, $M=N$, which is (b).

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7, proof of (1), printed pp.158-159: comparison of an arbitrary Cartesian edge with a marked lift via the 2-simplex and the type (3) generator; HTT Corollary 3.1.1.7 for the two-out-of-three on the triangle.

proof.text: Conversely assume (b), so $(X,M)=X^\natural$ for the cartesian fibration $X\to S$. A member of $J_S$ of type (i), (ii) or (iii) is a map over $S$ whose underlying marked map is one of the generators of the marked-anodyne class of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], hence a marked-anodyne map over $S$ in the sense of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]. The first clause of that node gives $X^\natural\to S^\sharp$ the right lifting property against it; a diagonal of a square over $S^\sharp$ is a marked diagonal over $S$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7, proof of (1), p.158 (the factorization j_X by generators (1)-(3)); Proposition 3.1.1.6, 'if' direction, and Remark 3.1.1.10.

proof.text: Still assuming (b), let a square be given with left side $A_s^\flat\to A_s$, both base maps constant at $s$. Its top map $A^\flat\to(X,M)$ lies over the constant map, so it lands in $(X_s,M_s)$. Since $M=N$, Step 2(2) shows that $X_s$ is a quasicategory and $M_s$ is exactly its set of equivalences, that is, $(X_s,M_s)=(X_s)^\natural$. The 'if' direction of [lem-coef-finite-marked-fibrancy-criterion] gives $(X_s,M_s)\to(\Delta^0)^\sharp$ the right lifting property against $A^\flat\to A$; the resulting marked map $A\to X_s\subseteq X$ is a diagonal over $S$ because both base maps are constant at $s$. With Step 4 this proves (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), and Steps 1-3 prove (a)$\Rightarrow$(b).

split_report.summary: Split the finite relative lifting recognition into five proof steps following HTT 3.1.3.7(1). Step 1 reads the generators (i), (ii) as inner fibration, cartesian lifts and cartesian marked edges. Step 2 identifies, on each vertex fiber, the marking M with the equivalences under (a) via the finite point criterion, and the cartesian edges with the equivalences for any cartesian fibration via the pullback clause and the point characterization. Step 3 shows every cartesian edge is marked using the triangle two-out-of-three lemma, the fiber identification and generator (iii). Steps 4-5 give the converse from the relative marked-anodyne lifting and the point criterion. Maintainer reader (Q95 review) rewrote Steps 2, 3 and 5: the fiber equivalence the source asserts without proof, the extension over A, and the converse detector were previously uncited or used the point criterion in the wrong direction; the fix cites the existing node lem-coef-marked-triangle-cancellation. No new nodes.
